nodes.title: RIFE / generic DNN frame interpolation
widgets_values:
RIFE FRAME INTERPOLATION THROUGH THE GENERIC cv2.dnn NODES

Model (download it yourself - models are machine state, not repo state):
  https://huggingface.co/FuryTMP/RIFE_v4.9
    rife_v4.9.onnx   21 MB, fp32, MIT
  Drop it into ComfyUI/models/onnx (if your extra_model_paths.yaml
  repoints that directory elsewhere, it must go THERE instead).
  RIFE: Huang et al., ECCV 2022 (arXiv 2011.06294), MIT.

NOT the fp32 export at huggingface.co/FuryTMP/RIFE_fp32: it LOADS on the
new graph engine and then dies in forward() with an int64-meets-float32
mismatch in nary_eltwise_layers.cpp, on every size and every engine
(classic cannot even parse it). It works fine under onnxruntime - cv2.dnn
just cannot run that graph. Its 7th channel is also ignored, so t would
have been stuck at 0.5.

THE MODEL'S CONTRACT, all measured on this OpenCV 5.0.0 build:
  * ONE input, (1, 7, H, W) float32: frame A RGB, frame B RGB, then a
    plane filled with the timestep t. Values are 0..1 - feeding 0..255
    returns a saturated picture instead of raising.
  * t is REAL: t=0 returns frame A, t=1 returns frame B, and the frames
    in between move smoothly. Set it on the subgraph to place the new
    frame anywhere, not just half way.
  * H and W must be MULTIPLES OF 32. The subgraph pads with
    BORDER_REPLICATE and crops back ('CV Slice Array'). Padding beats
    resizing: 2.86 vs 3.84 mean abs error on the clip below.
  * batch is 1 - a 2-pair blob dies in reshape2_layer, same as RAFT.
    One pair per execution; loop for more.
  * ENGINE = NEW GRAPH. Classic cannot parse the graph and the default
    engine picks classic. (ENGINE_ORT works too.)

WHEN TO USE IT INSTEAD OF 'CV Flow Interpolate (Video)' - measured against
held-out real frames (MAE) and synthvideo ground truth:
                          DIS        RIFE 4.9
  gap 1 (small motion)    1.32        1.56      DIS wins
  gap 4                   3.29        2.76      RIFE wins
  gap 8                   5.02        4.21      RIFE wins
  object at 32 px/frame   2.27        0.96      RIFE wins (SSIM .939/.984)
  cost per pair           0.009 s     0.02-0.12 s
DIS is better AND ~10x cheaper while the motion is small; RIFE takes over
as soon as it is large, which is where warp-and-blend tears. Neither
dominates, so both ship and the DIS video blueprint is unchanged.

THIS GRAPH: frames 0 and 2 go in, frame 1 is held out as ground truth.
Row 1 RIFE, row 2 the real frame, row 3 a cross-fade, row 4 PSNR for both
against the truth, row 5 the same pair at t=0.25 and t=0.75.
